summary: Spec fidelity (checker.md section 2: 'One owner per pass condition ... L0.ok-exit owns the exit equals the code's registered exit'; the section's own reading of the tables: an exit 2 in a row is shorthand for refused with a code whose registered exit is 2, the row asserts the code): L2.input-refusals (input.rs:206), L2.input-tty (241), L2.input-conflict (359), L2.input-pointer (436, 448), L2.batch-preflight (513) and the document numbers of L1.numbers (668) test the literal exit 2 as well as the code. Probe: a wrapper that answers every INPUT_INVALID of an --input call with exit 1 and leaves the envelope as it is fails L0.ok-exit (the owner: 'failed with INPUT_INVALID and exited 1, the registry says 2') and also L2.input-refusals, L2.input-tty and L1.numbers; the wrapper also dirtied L0.unknown-command-text and L1.fields through its own $() capture, which is the wrapper's doing and not counted here. The L1 rows have the same habit (Judge::refused, l1.rs:171), so this is a continuation of an existing convention, not a new one, but the 7.2 table wants one owner. Blast radius: one exit-number mistake fails four to six checks and the report no longer says which one owns it.
